selected_problem: After canonicalizing evidence bytes to HEAD, evidence path discovery still begins from mutable working-tree `evidence/*.json`. A dirty deletion of a committed evidence file, or of the whole evidence directory, can therefore erase a canonical-main unresolved boundary from autonomous diagnosis before HEAD content is ever read.

execution.route_basis: Fresh main exposes one narrow, falsifiable continuation of the canonical-main observation invariant: bytes are already HEAD-bound but path enumeration is not. The defect is local, high-centrality, evidence-dense and does not require any product or architecture decision, so source-contract replay routes to DEEP_DEVELOPMENT without forced mode rotation.

changes: Canonical evidence paths are now enumerated from `git ls-tree ... HEAD -- evidence` when HEAD is available, rather than from mutable working-tree directory contents.
A dirty deletion of a committed evidence JSON file cannot remove that canonical file from truth-boundary observation.
A dirty deletion of the entire working-tree evidence directory cannot erase canonical-main boundary discovery; non-Git fallback remains bounded to filesystem enumeration.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED against the prior canonical-byte logic: focused test 0/2 PASS. Deleting the committed evidence file, or deleting the whole evidence directory, produced RuntimeError: NO_ACTIONABLE_CANDIDATE even though HEAD still contained the unresolved boundary.

truth_boundaries: Canonical truth-boundary evidence is now HEAD-bound in both path enumeration and file bytes, but other closed-capability probes in `_probe_workspace` still inspect mutable working-tree source files.
Git HEAD provenance is not semantic or cryptographic proof that an evidence claim is correct.
The non-Git fallback intentionally retains filesystem enumeration because no canonical revision exists there.
BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so external GET-to-PUT base races remain outside client-side elimination.
